lane: DYNOTEARS: Andrey against CausalNex 0.12.2 and the empty window
build: Andrey pre-release build of the 0.13.0 branch, 31 October 2026
source: Pamfil et al. (2020), DYNOTEARS, AISTATS, arXiv 2002.00498v2: the simulations of Sect. 3 and Appendix B.4, at the settings of Appendix B.3
fit_protocol: one timed fit per series, no warm-up, one BLAS thread on one core, four fits at a time on four cores, a 3600 s wall cap per fit; andrey_cpu_s and comparator_cpu_s are the medians of the fits' CPU time, cpu_ratio the median over the paired series of CausalNex's CPU time over Andrey's, with its bootstrap 95% interval
error_metric: edge SHD over the window of lags 0 and 1: a same-step pair whose state differs (missing, extra, or reversed) costs 1, a lagged link in one graph and not the other costs 1 (lag0_shd + lagged_shd = shd); F1 of the directed edges, per block and over both; the _mean fields are means over the paired series
verdict_rule: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(CausalNex) per series on the series both finished; the mean D with its percentile bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 resamples); a setting in claim with at least 10 pairs is worse when the interval lies above 0, better when below, a tie otherwise; a worse setting is run again on 20 fresh seeds (20-39, the replication in its row) and counts as worse only if the replication's interval also lies above 0. Settings with claim 'out' are reported, not judged
seeds_note: 20 series per setting in claim (seeds 0-19), 10 per setting out of claim (seeds 0-9); replications on seeds 20-39

settings.n500: the paper's settings for 500 steps and Andrey's defaults: lambda1 0.05, w_threshold 0.3, lag_threshold 0.1, tau_max 1
settings.n50: the paper's settings for 50 steps: lambda1 0.2, w_threshold 0.3, lag_threshold 0.2, tau_max 1
settings.mapping: CausalNex from_pandas_dynamic(p=tau_max, lambda_w=lambda1, lambda_a=lambda1, max_iter=100, h_tol=1e-8, w_threshold=0.0), then same-step weights kept where abs(w) >= w_threshold and lagged weights where abs(a) >= lag_threshold; the centered arm fits X and the lagged Y centered on their column means with from_numpy_dynamic

regimes.dynotears_paper: Erdos-Renyi same-step graph of mean degree 2, Erdos-Renyi lagged graph of mean in-degree 2 with self-lags, Gaussian noise, raw scale (in claim)
regimes.dynotears_paper_exponential: the same graphs, exponential noise of scale 1 with its mean subtracted, raw scale (in claim)
regimes.dynotears_paper_ba_sbm: Barabasi-Albert same-step graph (2 edges per new node), two-block lagged graph of mean in-degree 2, Gaussian noise, raw scale, up to 50 variables (in claim)
regimes.dynotears_paper_standardized: dynotears_paper with every column z-scored (out of claim)
regimes.dynotears_paper_uncentered: exponential noise of mean 1, not centered (out of claim)
regimes.dynotears_sin_tanh: sin of each same-step parent and tanh of each lagged parent in place of the linear terms, Gaussian noise (out of claim)
regimes.length 50 at n500: dynotears_paper at 50 steps with the defaults (out of claim)

differences.500_steps: in claim, 34 of the 280 paired series end on a different graph; CausalNex on centered columns (fitted on those 34 alone) returns Andrey's graph on 29. Of the other 5, Andrey's graph changes on 4 when the data are multiplied by 1 + 1e-12 noise or the columns are fitted in their given order. On the fifth (exponential noise, 20 variables, seed 1) neither moves either package's graph; the one edge that differs is a true lagged edge of weight 0.10026 in Andrey's fit and 0.09975 in CausalNex's on centered columns, against the threshold 0.1, the largest weight difference between the two fits being 0.0048
differences.50_steps: every run has the centered arm (same_graph in each row's centered block). At 100 variables, on 4 exponential-noise series where Andrey's graph differs from CausalNex's on centered columns: Andrey stops on h_tol (h_final below 1e-8) with no edge removed by the cycle repair, refitting at rho_max 1e20 keeps the graph on 3 and matches CausalNex on none, and multiplying the data by 1 + 1e-12 noise changes the graph on 3 of the 4 (SHD -5, +4, -2; on one series to CausalNex's graph exactly), the columns in their given order on 2
